native_result.query: How does incarceration affect the wealth of black individuals based on their income levels?
native_result.HypoA: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.
native_result.HypoB: Among black NLSY79 respondents, being jailed sometime in 1985-1994 (ever_jailed=1) is associated with lower composite_wealth at 1985, 1990, and 1996 than never-jailed black respondents, with the gap widening over time (1996 medians: $0 vs $5,000; 1990: $0 vs $3,235). Since no income variable exists, income level is proxied by terciles of composite_wealth_1985; the negative association holds within every tercile (High tercile 1996 median $26,750 vs $4,700; all within-tercile Wilcoxon p<0.001). Controlling composite_wealth_1985 and sex, ever_jailed is negatively associated with 1996 wealth (coef ~ -$42,714, p=0.0008) and 1990 wealth (-$15,356 raw, p=0.13; -$16,464 winsorized, p<0.001). These are associations, not causal effects: jail isn't random, 1985 may overlap the jail window, and the jailed black sample is small (n=159), so selection/reverse causation cannot be ruled out.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load CSV (12013x6, no missing). 2) Descriptives by race/sex/ever_jailed. 3) Black-subgroup means/medians ever vs never per snapshot + Mann-Whitney. 4) Proxy income via 1985-wealth terciles (Low/Mid/High), within-tercile means/medians/gaps/n + tests. 5) OLS of 1990 and 1996 wealth on ever_jailed controlling 1985 wealth and sex, with 99th-percentile winsorized robustness.
